title: Telemetry cushion and schema-drift detector for graceful contract evolution
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Add a non-disruptive ‘cushion’ layer to the usage-event ingestion path that detects schema drift early, scores contract violations, and delays hard enforcement until a planned canary and backfill window completes. Scope: (1) lightweight schema profiler that computes per-field telemetry (presence, type distribution, cardinality) at ingestion time; (2) drift classifier that raises alerts when field-level distributions shift beyond configurable thresholds; (3) an enforcement policy engine with three modes: permissive (log+tag), cushion (queue for curated backfill + soft-coerce), and strict (reject). Why: recent customer regressions from abrupt schema changes show we need a graduated approach to keep Console dashboards and billing stable while allowing product teams to evolve events. Approach: stream a small sampling (1-5%) of events to the profiler; maintain 7/30/90-day baseline histograms; compute a drift score per event and aggregate per-tenant; when score > threshold, mark the event stream as ‘drifting’ and flip to cushion mode via feature flag. Cushion mode will: (a) attach metadata to events (schema_version, drift_score), (b) route ambiguous payloads to a separate ‘cushion’ Kafka topic for ephemeral storage, (c) trigger an automated backfill job to reprocess prior N days with relaxed coercion rules if the team approves. Acceptance criteria: (A) profiler adds <2ms p99 to sampled ingest path; (B) drift alerts surface in Console with example events and suggested remediation; (C) canary cushion rollout to 5 internal tenants without user-facing errors; (D) documented backfill and rollback playbook. Non-goals: full schema migration automation and user-facing schema editor for this sprint.
comments: 2026-02-05 - Kickoff: scoped MVP with Product (Sofia Chen) and Observability (Marcus Lee). Agreed sample-based profiler to keep path cheap.

2026-02-12 - Spike complete: prototype profiler implemented using Bloom-cardinality + histograms stored in ClickHouse; per-sample overhead ~0.6ms on dev cluster. Notes: need to trim cardinality windows for high-cardinal fields like request_id.
2026-02-20 - Design review: PM asked for clear UX in Console showing drift examples and 'accept change' workflow. Added requirement to include example payloads in alert card.
2026-02-27 - Trade-offs: strict enforcement reduces consumer breakage but increases error volume. We chose cushion-first approach to balance reliability and developer velocity.
2026-03-03 - Implementation: cushion topic created (kafka.topic.telemetry_cushion). Router change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876 (needs ops review).
2026-03-08 - Ops: added monitoring queries for cushion lag and cushion topic retention. Playbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/telemetry-cushion

2026-03-10 - QA: end-to-end tests added that simulate schema drift (field type flips, missing fields) and validate that cushion mode preserves downstream pipelines. Failing case: schema coercion for nested arrays; spike planned to handle nested-array heuristics.

Open questions: (1) What default thresholds are reasonable per-tenant? Suggest start: presence_change >15% OR type_change_ratio >5% triggers medium alert. (2) How long to keep cushion items before auto-expire? Current proposal: 7 days retention + backfill window. (3) Should billing derive from original or coerced shape while cushion is active? Need PM decision.

Next steps: (A) finish nested-array coercion spike (ENG-250001), (B) add Console alert cards + 'accept change' button, (C) run canary on 5 internal tenants for 2 weeks, (D) prepare runbook for backfill and rollback.
